newsitem.title: USA: Halifax start-up effort to affect Q1 1998.
newsitem.headline: Halifax start-up effort to affect Q1 1998.

text.p: Halifax Corp said that it was confident about the ultimate success of its new printer maintanance business, but start-up costs will affect the first quarter of fiscal 1998.

Howard Mills, president of the technology and facilities services company, said that, as it forecast, its income for the fourth quarter 1977 that ended March 31 had been "minimal" due to large start-up costs on new large contracts for printer maintainance.
Otherwise, he noted, the company was pleased with its results for the fiscal year, which he said confirmed continued growth.
The company said net income for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended March 31 was $7,000 and $954,000, respectively, on revenues of $18.194 million and $76.278 million.
Primary share earnings were nil for the fourth quarter and $0.47 for the fourth quarter and fiscal year periods.

It said net income for the same periods in the prior year was $357,000 or $0.20 a share and $763,000 or $0.43 a share on revenues of $17.920 million and $47.159 million. Fully diluted earnings per share for fiscal year 1997 were $0.46.
